primary_meaning: People belonging to God—especially disciples or believers whose spiritual life and fruitfulness depend on union with Christ, the vine.
primary_basis: John 15:1–6 — Jesus identifies himself as the true vine and his disciples as the branches; abiding in him produces fruit.
John 15:8,16 — fruitful branches are associated with faithful discipleship.
Romans 11:16–24 — natural and grafted branches represent Jewish and Gentile participants in the covenant people, dependent on the sustaining root.

alternatives.meaning: Israel, Jewish people, and Gentiles in relation to the covenant community; branches may be retained, broken off, or grafted in.
The Messiah or Davidic king as a new shoot or 'Branch' arising from Jesse or David.
Descendants, offspring, or an extending family line.
Kingdoms, rulers, nations, or their expanding power, represented by branches of a symbolic tree.
Visible growth, works, influence, or fruitfulness flowing from an underlying spiritual source.

notes: Christian teaching most recognizably associates branches with believers abiding in Christ because of John 15. However, the Bible uses branch imagery in several materially different ways, so there is no single context-independent symbolic definition. The singular title 'the Branch' is especially associated with the Messiah and should not automatically determine the meaning of plural 'branches' in other passages.
